Insality/druid

Entry point for Druid UI Framework. Create a new Druid instance and adjust the Druid settings here.

  • GitHub: Insality/druid — pinned to 1.4.2
    1. Pick a release from Insality/druid releases and add its Source code (zip) URL (or a packaged .zip asset, if the library ships one) to game.project under [project] dependencies, then Fetch Libraries in the Defold editor.
    2. Run bunx @defold-typescript/cli resolve to materialize its types.
    3. Import it under a namespace alias of your choice:

new(context: LuaTable, style?: LuaTable | undefined): druid_instance

Create a new Druid instance for creating GUI components.

Parameters

  • context: LuaTable — The Druid context. Usually, this is the self of the gui_script. It is passed into all Druid callbacks.
  • style?: LuaTable | undefined — The Druid style table to override style parameters for this Druid instance.

Returns

  • druid_instance — The new Druid instance

register(name: string, module: LuaTable)

Register a new external Druid component. Register component just makes the druid:new_{name} function. For example, if you register a component called "my_component", you can create it using druid:new_my_component(...). This can be useful if you have your own "basic" components that you don't want to require in every file. The default way to create component is druid_instance:new(component_class, ...).

Parameters

  • name: string — Module name
  • module: LuaTable — Lua table with component

set_default_style(style: LuaTable)

Set the default style for all Druid instances.

Parameters

  • style: LuaTable — Default style

set_text_function(callback: (text_id: string) => string)

Set the text function for the LangText component.

Parameters

  • callback: (text_id: string) => string — Get localized text function

set_sound_function(callback: (sound_id: string) => void)

Set the sound function to able components to play sounds.

Parameters

  • callback: (sound_id: string) => void — Sound play callback

init_window_listener()

Subscribe Druid to the window listener. It will override your previous window listener, so if you have one, you should call M.on_window_callback manually.

on_window_callback(window_event: Opaque<"constant">)

Set the window callback to enable Druid window events.

Parameters

  • window_event: Opaque<"constant"> — Event param from window listener

on_language_change()

Call this function when the game language changes. It will notify all Druid instances to update the lang text components.

get_druid(gui_url?: Url | string | undefined): druid_instance | undefined

Get the Druid instance bound to the GUI by druid.register_druid_as_widget(). Unlike druid.get_widget(), the instance is returned as is, without cross-context events wrapping, so from a game object script you should only use its plain functions, not the GUI related ones. local instance = druid.get_druid("gui_widget") instance:set_style(my_style) -- Should be set before creating widgets

Parameters

  • gui_url?: Url | string | undefined — GUI url or string of component name near current script

Returns

  • druid_instance | undefined — The registered Druid instance or nil if not registered

get_widget<T extends druid_widget>(widget_class: T, gui_url: Url | string, params?: unknown | undefined, template?: string | undefined): T

Create a widget from the bound Druid GUI instance. The widget will be created and all widget functions can be called from Game Object contexts. This allows using only druid_widget.gui_script for GUI files and call this widget functions from Game Object script file. Widget class here is your lua file for the GUI scene (widgets in Druid) msg.url(nil, nil, "gui_widget") -- current game object msg.url(nil, object_url, "gui_widget") -- other game object

Parameters

  • widget_class: T — The class of the widget to return
  • gui_url: Url | string — GUI url or string of component name near current script
  • params?: unknown | undefined — Additional parameters to pass to the widget's init function
  • template?: string | undefined — The GUI template name used by the widget nodes

Returns

  • T — The new created widget,

register_druid_as_widget(druid: druid_instance)

Bind a Druid GUI instance to the current game object. This instance now can produce widgets from druid.get_widget() function. Only one widget can be set per game object.

Parameters

  • druid: druid_instance — The druid instance to register

unregister_druid_as_widget()

Should be called on final, where druid instance is destroyed.

druid_rich_text.set_text(text?: string | undefined): LuaMultiReturn<[druid_rich_text_word[], druid_rich_text_lines_metrics]>

Set text for Rich Text -- Color rich_text:set_text("＜color=red＞Foobar＜/color＞") rich_text:set_text("＜color=1.0,0,0,1.0＞Foobar＜/color＞") rich_text:set_text("＜color=#ff0000＞Foobar＜/color＞") rich_text:set_text("＜color=#ff0000ff＞Foobar＜/color＞") -- Shadow rich_text:set_text("＜shadow=red＞Foobar＜/shadow＞") rich_text:set_text("＜shadow=1.0,0,0,1.0＞Foobar＜/shadow＞") rich_text:set_text("＜shadow=#ff0000＞Foobar＜/shadow＞") rich_text:set_text("＜shadow=#ff0000ff＞Foobar＜/shadow＞") -- Outline rich_text:set_text("＜outline=red＞Foobar＜/outline＞") rich_text:set_text("＜outline=1.0,0,0,1.0＞Foobar＜/outline＞") rich_text:set_text("＜outline=#ff0000＞Foobar＜/outline＞") rich_text:set_text("＜outline=#ff0000ff＞Foobar＜/outline＞") -- Font rich_text:set_text("＜font=MyCoolFont＞Foobar＜/font＞") -- Size rich_text:set_text("＜size=2＞Twice as large＜/size＞") -- Line break rich_text:set_text("＜br/＞Insert a line break") -- No break rich_text:set_text("＜nobr＞Prevent the text from breaking") -- Image rich_text:set_text("＜img=texture:image＞Display image") rich_text:set_text("＜img=texture:image,size＞Display image with size") rich_text:set_text("＜img=texture:image,width,height＞Display image with width and height")

Parameters

  • text?: string | undefined — The text to set

Returns

  • druid_rich_text_word[]
  • druid_rich_text_lines_metrics

action

action.value: number

The amount of input given by the user. This is usually 1 for buttons and 0-1 for analogue inputs. This is not present for mouse movement.

action.pressed: boolean

If the input was pressed this frame. This is not present for mouse movement.

action.released: boolean

If the input was released this frame. This is not present for mouse movement.

action.repeated: boolean

If the input was repeated this frame. This is similar to how a key on a keyboard is repeated when you hold it down. This is not present for mouse movement.

action.x: number

The x value of a pointer device, if present.

action.y: number

The y value of a pointer device, if present.

action.screen_x: number

The screen space x value of a pointer device, if present.

action.screen_y: number

The screen space y value of a pointer device, if present.

action.dx: number

The change in x value of a pointer device, if present.

action.dy: number

The change in y value of a pointer device, if present.

action.screen_dx: number

The change in screen space x value of a pointer device, if present.

action.screen_dy: number

The change in screen space y value of a pointer device, if present.

action.gamepad: number

The index of the gamepad device that provided the input.

action.touch: touch[]

List of touch input, one element per finger, if present. See table below about touch input

action.text: string

The text input.

touch

touch.id: number

A number identifying the touch input during its duration.

touch.pressed: boolean

True if the finger was pressed this frame.

touch.released: boolean

True if the finger was released this frame.

touch.tap_count: number

Number of taps, one for single, two for double-tap, etc

touch.x: number

The x touch location.

touch.y: number

The y touch location.

touch.dx: number

The change in x value.

touch.dy: number

The change in y value.

touch.acc_x: number | undefined

Accelerometer x value (if present).

touch.acc_y: number | undefined

Accelerometer y value (if present).

touch.acc_z: number | undefined

druid_instance.set_whitelist(whitelist_components?: LuaTable | druid_component[] | undefined): druid_instance

Set whitelist components for input processing. If whitelist is set, only the listed components and their descendants receive input. An empty list allows none. Pass nil to clear the whitelist (all components receive input). Descendants created later still match, no need to call this again.

The filter is scoped to the caller: on the druid instance it affects all components, on the self.druid inside a component it affects this component subtree only. The filter owner is not affected by its own filter, so a widget can restrict its children and keep its own on_input working.

Parameters

  • whitelist_components?: LuaTable | druid_component[] | undefined — The array of component to whitelist, nil to clear it

Returns

  • druid_instance — The Druid instance

druid_instance.set_blacklist(blacklist_components?: LuaTable | druid_component[] | undefined): druid_instance

Set blacklist components for input processing. If blacklist is set, the listed components and their descendants are skipped on the input step. An empty list and nil both deny nobody. Descendants created later still match.

The filter is scoped to the caller: on the druid instance it affects all components, on the self.druid inside a component it affects this component subtree only. The filter owner is not affected by its own filter, to filter a widget itself set the filter from the outside: the gui script or the parent widget.

Parameters

  • blacklist_components?: LuaTable | druid_component[] | undefined — The array of component to blacklist, nil to clear it

Returns

  • druid_instance — The Druid instance

druid_instance.reset_hovers(): druid_instance

Reset the hover state of all hover components of the Druid instance. The hovers trigger the hover events with false and drop their cursors. Call it when another GUI covers this one and takes the input: the covered nodes never get the mouse leave. The next pointer move over a node hovers it again.

Returns

  • druid_instance — The Druid instance
